newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- President Nelson Mandela will chair the peace talks between Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila starting on Friday on board the SA Navy auxiliary vessel, Outeniqua.

- The 100 percent sale of Sun Air, SA's first full privatisation exercise, should be completed by the end of July, with eight local and international consortiums having qualified to bid for the arline, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said.
- The death rate of SA employees was expected to increase four to five times in the next decade as the HIV/AIDS epidemic progressed, Southern Life said.
BUSINESS REPORT

- A range of industrial developments costing billions of rands have been earmarked for Durban, Richards Bay and Pietermaritzburg, Jacob Zuma, the KwaZulu Natal tourism and economic affairs minister, said.
- Records tumbled on the JSE as gold shares crashed, industrial and financial shares powered ahead and volumes reached ndw heights, dealers said.

- The public enterprises and transport departments named the eight companies and consortiums which had prequalified to make a bid for the state-owned Sun Air, which is to be fully privatised by the end of July.
SAKE BEELD

- Plans to privatise Safcol, the state-owned forestry company, have been suspended amid uncertainty about the future of goverment's forestry interests in the former homeland areas which are becoming increasingly run down.
- The government has started an investigation into the large number of concerns which are exempt from paying tax. Especially sporting organisations are being targeted by the Receiver of Revenue.
- Virgin Atlantic and Malaysia Air are amongst the eight consortiums shortlisted for the privatisation of Sun Air.
THE STAR

- South Africa has called in the navy to try to end the wr in Zaire, persuading Zairian President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila to hold their first face-to-face meeting aboard an SA Navy ship in the Atlantic under the chairmanship of President Nelson Mandela.

- Pretoria murder and robbery detectives cannot link the killing of two men on a Diepsloot small holding, north of Johannesburg, at the weekend to the murders of two other people on smallholdings in the earea earlier this year.
- The Guinness flowed thick and fast in Dublin, the Irish capital, on Tuesday after South African cricket captain Hansie Cronje led an Irish XI to its first-ever victory over an English county side.

- The government has forecast major breakthroughs in the Reconstruction and Development Programme this year, including 200,000 new houses and school meals for five million pupils a day by the end of the year.
